items.title: 68251_Teddy McRae oral history interview
items.q: [INTERVIEWER] How about, say, Mr. Small and Mr. Wilkin's ability to maintain these clubs. ... [INTERVIEWEE] Oh yeah. Small's Paradise was right on the same level as the Cotton Club was on.

ctx.x: Just like some of these rock groups, man, they come up and they make all this bread and (inaudible). Just too much money. Have all this service given to them -- limousines. We didn't have that back there. We had nothing like that in those days. We had like -- we had to work it, we had to make it.
How about, say, Mr. Small and Mr. Wilkin's ability to maintain these clubs. They managed all right, apparently.

Oh yeah. Small's Paradise was right on the same level as the Cotton Club was on. They had people in those clubs -- It wasn't no headache for them. They had people that were taking care of the crowd. They had, like, strong-armed guys. Bouncers back there. They had bouncers. They had people that people respected.
